# Draft (create mode)

**Title (new):** Report delivery: empty first emailed download, missing final row, duplicate emails, wrong date in subject

## Context

Users get reports in two ways: they download them, or they have them emailed. A customer support review surfaced four separate problems with how those reports reach recipients.

One mechanism detail was supplied with the request. The export job writes the report file and passes it to the outgoing-email queue before it knows how many rows the report has. (The outgoing-email queue is where messages wait before they are sent.) This ticket records that ordering as context only. It does not claim the ordering causes any of the failures below. (Pointer for the implementer: deliveryMux calls writeRows, then sendMail.)

## Problem

Each failure below was observed separately.

**1. The first emailed download is empty, so the recipient has to try again.**
The recipient opens the emailed report, finds nothing in it, and has to come back later.
Example: a 12-row report downloads as zero rows the first time. A later retry gives all 12 rows.

**2. Downloads leave out the final row, so recipients work from incomplete totals.**
The file looks complete, but the last line is missing. Any total calculated from it is wrong.
Example: a report shows four rows on screen but downloads as three. The fourth row exists, but the file leaves it out.

**3. Recipients get the same email twice and have to check whether the two reports differ.**
Example: one delivery request sends two emails. Both carry the same file.

**4. The email subject names the previous day, so recipients file today's report under yesterday.**
Example: a report requested on October 21 arrives with an October 20 subject line. The attached file is correctly dated October 21.

## Idea

Reporter proposes fixing report delivery so each failure above stops occurring.

## Acceptance Criteria

The criteria are grouped by failure. They stay in one ticket because no evidence was supplied that the fixes can ship independently.

**Failure 1: empty first emailed download**
- [ ] Given a report with 12 rows that is requested for email delivery, when the recipient opens the first emailed download, the file contains 12 rows.

**Failure 2: missing final row**
- [ ] Given a report that shows four rows on screen, when the report is downloaded, the file contains all four rows.

**Failure 3: duplicate email**
- [ ] Given one email delivery request for a report, when the request is processed, exactly one email is sent.

**Failure 4: wrong date in subject**
- [ ] Given an email delivery request made on October 21, when the email is sent, its subject names October 21.

*(No Out of scope / Follow-up section and no Post-deployment housekeeping section: neither has any content. No Reporter-note comment is proposed, because the Idea section holds the single sketch line and nothing was left over.)*

---

# AC integrity gate report (assembled draft)

**Normalization:** The four required outcomes were rewritten as `- [ ]` items. No criterion was skipped because of how it was phrased.

| # | AC (abridged) | Structural class | Setup / action / observable | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First emailed download of a 12-row report has 12 rows | Behavioral (binary) | 12-row report, email delivery / open first download / 12 rows present | **Pass** |
| 2 | Download of a 4-row report has all 4 rows | Behavioral; the full set of rows can be listed today (the four rows on screen), so it is not a vague "all X" claim | Report showing 4 rows / download / 4 rows in file | **Pass** |
| 3 | One delivery request sends one email | Behavioral (binary) | One email request / process it / exactly one email sent | **Pass** |
| 4 | October 21 request has an October 21 subject | Behavioral (binary) | Request dated October 21 / send / subject names October 21 | **Pass** |

**Defect classes found:**
- Wishful: none.
- Tautological: none.
- Unspecified-but-binding: none.
- External-input dependency: none.
- Post-deployment: none.

**Deploy-window check:**
- All four ACs can be verified before production deployment using representative data.
- No AC names an environment.
- No AC was moved to Post-deployment housekeeping.

**Guards:**
- Every number and date (12 rows, four rows, one email, October 21) comes from the examples supplied in the request. Nothing was invented.
- No baselines were needed, because none of the ACs is comparative.
- The mail-queue ordering detail stays in Context as a pointer. It is not turned into an AC or presented as a confirmed root cause.

**Gate result:** **PASS.** There is no hard stop and nothing to park, so the ticket can be filed as ready.

**Note for step 5 (split detection):** The four failures are independent, but no split is proposed. As instructed, they stay in one ticket with an AC group per failure, because no evidence was supplied that the fixes can ship separately.

## Replacement ticket body

## Context

A customer support review identified four failures in report delivery. Customers can download reports or receive them by email.

## Problem

- **The first download of an emailed report is empty, forcing the recipient to retry.** A report with 12 rows downloads as zero rows on the first attempt; retrying later returns all 12 rows.
- **Downloads omit the final row, leaving recipients with incomplete totals.** A report with four rows downloads as three rows, even though the fourth row appears on screen.
- **A single delivery request sends duplicate emails, making recipients check whether the reports differ.** One request sends two emails containing the same file.
- **The email subject names the previous day’s report, causing recipients to misfile current work.** An October 21 request produces an October 20 subject even though the file is the October 21 report.

## Idea

Reporter proposal: Fix report delivery so the first download is complete, the final row is included, each email delivery request sends one email, and the subject names the requested report’s date.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a report containing 12 rows, when email delivery is requested and the recipient downloads the report for the first time, that first download contains all 12 rows without a retry.
- [ ] Given a report with four rows visible on screen, when the report is downloaded, the downloaded file contains all four rows, including the fourth row.
- [ ] Given a report and one email delivery request, when that request is processed, the recipient receives exactly one report email.
- [ ] Given an October 21 report, when email delivery is requested on October 21, the email subject names October 21 rather than October 20.

---

## AC integrity gate report

**Result: PASS — no hard stop, parking requirement, or relocation.**

| AC | Classification | Gate result |
|---|---|---|
| First download contains 12 rows | Behavioral | Supplied 12-row setup, first-download action, and exact expected row count. |
| Download includes the fourth row | Behavioral; finite completeness check | The required set is enumerable today: the four rows visible on screen. Download must contain all four. |
| One request sends one email | Behavioral | One request is the setup and action; exactly one received email is the observable result. |
| Subject names October 21 | Behavioral | Supplied report date and request date; the subject’s expected date is explicit. |

- All criteria are unchecked checklist items with setup, action, and observable results.
- All are verifiable before production deployment; none requires a production-only observation or names a test environment.
- Counts and dates come from the supplied examples; no measurements or thresholds were invented.
- **Wording check:** Each failure has a plain-language impact and concrete example. Context, Problem, and Idea are understandable without code references.
- **Split:** Not proposed. The four outcomes remain in one ticket; independent shipping evidence was not supplied.
- **Comment:** None proposed; there is no overflow proposal material.
